title: Jensen Huang on extreme co-design, shaping belief, speed-of-light thinking and resilience (Lex Fridman #494)
summary: Jensen explains why Nvidia moved from chips to rack and AI-factory scale design, and how he builds a company around the output. He covers betting CUDA on GeForce, pre-shaping belief before big announcements, first-principles "speed of light" thinking, and handling suffering by decomposing problems. He also gives career advice on AI and jobs.

principles.text: Design the company's structure around the output it must produce, not a copied org chart.
principles.quote: the goal of au of a company is to be the machinery, the mechanism, the system that produces the output and that output is the product that we like to create.

principles.text: Run a flat org: large direct staff, no one-on-ones, problems attacked in the open by everyone.
principles.quote: My direct staff is 60 people. You know, I don't have one-on-ones with them because it's impossible.

principles.text: Install base is the most important property of a computing platform, so seed it even at great cost.
principles.quote: install base defines an architecture not everything else is secondary.

principles.text: Shape belief with everyone daily so the big announcement feels obvious, not shocking.
principles.quote: I'm trying to shape their belief system such that when I come the day I say, "Hey, let's buy Melanox." It's completely obvious to everybody that we absolutely should.

principles.text: Break pressure into parts, tell someone who can act, forget setbacks, and keep moving.
principles.quote: I decompose the problem. I reason about the problem and I I share the load with it.

principles.text: Jobs have purposes that outlast the tasks AI automates; learn to use AI.
principles.quote: the purpose of your job and the tasks and the tools that you use to do your job are related, not the same.
